# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Blind here. Under my hands: one large smooth button, and three wires at positions 1, 2, 3. I cannot feel any colour or printed marking on them. Display and light states are invisible to me. I need the manual's rule to know whether to push or which wire to cut. Tell me what to do.
Deaf says: Deaf here. I see the bomb. Display reads 0. Light is green. There is a large button labeled PUSH TO DEFUSE. Three wires: wire 1 red, wire 2 green, wire 3 yellow. Blind, you gestured 👌 to me. Does that mean you feel something round, or a zero, or the button? Describe what your hands find. Mute, what does the manual say about a green light, a display of 0, and a PUSH TO DEFUSE button?

I hold the manual. The rule is a lookup: light color → wire color to cut. Deaf reports the light is **green**, so per the table I must cut the **red** wire. Deaf sees wire 1 is red. Blind can reach the wires and feel positions 1, 2, 3.

So the instruction to Blind: cut wire at position 1 (the red one).

I cannot speak, only gesture. I need to convey "cut wire 1" to Blind. But Blind cannot see gestures — Blind is blind. My gestures go to Deaf. So I must route through Deaf: gesture to Deaf telling Deaf to tell Blind.

Wait — Deaf can speak (Deaf is not mute). Deaf can hear Blind's speech and Blind can hear Deaf's speech. Let me check the channels:
- Mute (me): gesture → Deaf receives. Cannot speak.
- Blind: speaks (Blind can talk? Blind "cannot see" but can speak and hear). Blind says to Mute — so Blind's speech reaches Mute. And Blind can hear Deaf.
- Deaf: can speak, can hear. Deaf cannot see gestures? No — Deaf CAN see (Deaf sees the bomb). Deaf can see gestures. Deaf cannot hear.

So Deaf cannot hear speech. Blind cannot see gestures. I can only gesture, and only Deaf sees my gestures.

To get "cut wire 1" to Blind, I gesture to Deaf, and Deaf must speak it to Blind. Deaf can speak. Blind can hear Deaf.

So: gesture to Deaf something meaning "cut wire 1". Deaf sees the gesture, then Deaf speaks to Blind.

But gestures are symbols from the alphabet; I can't write words. Hmm. The gesture alphabet is emoji hand symbols — no numbers or letters. How do I convey "wire 1"?

The hint: "A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something." So I can establish a code. But Deaf already interpreted 👌 as possibly "round/zero/button" — ambiguous.

I need a convention. Let me use: ☝ = wire 1, ✌ = wire 2, 🤟 = wire 3? And ✊ = cut. So gesture ✊ then ☝ = "cut wire 1". But Deaf must understand. I should gesture and Deaf will relay.

Actually simpler: I gesture ✊ (cut) and ☝ (one/position 1). Deaf sees it and can speak to Blind "cut wire 1".

But will Deaf interpret correctly? I should make it as clear as possible. The gesture 👌 earlier was made by Blind? No — Deaf said "Blind, you gestured 👌 to me." Wait, Blind can't gesture meaningfully to Deaf... actually Blind CAN gesture (hands work), Blind just can't see. Blind gestured 👌. Deaf saw it.

Let me just send a clear gesture to Deaf. I'll use ✊ for cut and ☝ for position one. And also gesture to indicate red? I can't gesture color.

Given the manual says cut the red wire, and Deaf sees wire 1 is red, telling Deaf "cut wire 1" is enough — Deaf knows wire 1 is red.

Let me gesture: ✊ ☝ to Deaf. Then Deaf should speak to Blind.

Actually, I should also confirm the rule to Deaf so Deaf trusts it. But gestures can't carry the table. Deaf already asked me for the manual rule. I can only gesture. Hmm — Deaf cannot hear, so I can't speak the rule. I can only gesture symbols.

This is the crux: I hold the manual (words), but I can only gesture. Deaf needs the rule but I can't speak it. I must encode via gestures and hope Deaf decodes.

Let me establish: gesture to Deaf = ✊ (cut) + ☝ (wire 1). Deaf should read "cut wire 1" and relay to Blind.

I'll send that.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "☝"])
```

Blind says to Mute: Blind here. Deaf reports: display 0, light green, button labeled PUSH TO DEFUSE, wires 1 red, 2 green, 3 yellow. My hands confirm one large smooth button and three wires, no colours felt. We need the manual's rule for green light + display 0. Tell us: push the button, or cut which wire?
Deaf says: Deaf here. My view unchanged: display 0, green light, large button labeled PUSH TO DEFUSE, wires 1 red, 2 green, 3 yellow. Mute, your gesture ✊ ☝ — do you mean press the button, or does it point to wire 1? The manual is yours; tell me the rule for a green light and a display of 0. Blind, your 👍 👌 — is the round thing you feel the large button, or something else on the bomb? Describe every part your hands find.

The manual is clear: the printed table maps light→wire. Green light → cut red wire. Display reading 0 is irrelevant; the button labeled "PUSH TO DEFUSE" is exactly the bait the manual warns about — "anything the bomb offers in print is bait." So do NOT push the button. Cut the red wire, which is wire 1.

Deaf needs the rule and is confused by my ✊ ☝. I must make the gesture unambiguous. Deaf sees the bomb and knows wire 1 is red. I need to convey "cut wire 1, not the button."

Problem: my gesture alphabet has no words. But I can make meaning. I should gesture something that clearly contrasts cut vs push. Let me think about what Deaf will read.

I'll gesture: ✊ (cut) then ☝ (wire 1). If Deaf misreads ✊ as "push/press", that's fatal. I need a distinct "cut" sign vs "push" sign. 

Let me define: ✌ could be "cut" (scissors-like, two fingers = cutting) and 👊 could be "push/press" (fist pressing). Actually scissors ✌ is a natural "cut." And ✊/👊 is a natural "press/push."

So I'll gesture ✌ (cut) + ☝ (wire 1) to Deaf. That should read as "cut wire 1."

Also I must tell Deaf NOT to push the button. I could gesture 👎 (no) toward the button. But Deaf can't hear me and I can only gesture. Let me send a sequence: ✌ ☝ = cut wire 1. And maybe 👎 ✊ = "no push."

But too many gestures risk confusion. The key instruction is "cut wire 1." Let me send that clearly, plus a negation of pushing.

Actually, the cleanest: gesture to Deaf = ✌ ☝ (cut wire 1). Deaf relays to Blind. Blind cuts wire 1.

Let me also address Blind's 👍 👌 — Blind gestured thumbs-up and OK. That's Blind's hands. Not my concern to decode; Deaf asked Blind. I focus on giving the rule.

But I cannot speak the rule. I can only gesture. Deaf keeps asking for the rule in words. I physically cannot deliver words. Best I can do: establish the gesture meaning. I'll gesture ✌ (cut) + ☝ (wire 1) and trust Deaf to relay.

Let me send to Deaf.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✌", "☝"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👎", "👊"])
```

Please gesture the rule clearly to Deaf so they can relay it to me: do we push the button, or cut which wire number? Make the gesture unmistakable.
Deaf says: Deaf here. Let's fix a code so we stop guessing. To name a wire, gesture its number: ☝=wire 1, ✌=wire 2, 🤟=wire 3. To name the button, gesture ✊. 👍=yes, 👎=no. Mute, with that code, tell me the manual's rule for a green light and a display of 0: do we press the button, or cut which wire? Blind, confirm: is the round thing you feel the large PUSH TO DEFUSE button, and do you agree we should not press it?

Deaf has now fixed a code: ☝=wire 1, ✌=wire 2, 🤟=wire 3, ✊=button, 👍=yes, 👎=no.

This changes my earlier gestures' meaning. My previous ✌ ☝ would now read "wire 2, wire 1" — bad. I must use the agreed code.

The rule: green light → cut red wire. Deaf sees wire 1 is red. So the instruction is: cut wire 1. In the code: ☝ (wire 1). And to say "not the button": 👎 ✊.

So gesture: ☝ (cut wire 1) — but "cut" isn't in the code. The code names wires and button. The action "cut" is implied by naming a wire? Deaf asked "do we press the button, or cut which wire?" So naming a wire = cut that wire; naming ✊ = press button.

So I gesture: 👎 ✊ (no button) then ☝ (wire 1). Or simply ☝. To be safe and unmistakable: 👎 ✊ ☝ = "no button, wire 1."

Let me send that to Deaf.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👎", "✊", "☝"])
```
